title: 7-Year Treasury Note auction — the January block's last leg, the day after the FOMC decision
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by THIS event's initial research and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream — a second independent read of the same primary, after the sibling proposal this file supersedes. Row reads verbatim `7-Year NOTE Thursday, January 21, 2027 Thursday, January 28, 2027 Monday, February 01, 2027` with NO trailing `R`; the flag column IS populated within twenty rows of it (`20-Year BOND R`, `10-Year TIPS T`), so the blank is a positive signal of a new issue, not a missing field. The AUCTION TIME is sourced rather than assumed: fiscaldata auctions_query publishes `closing_time_comp`, which reads `01:00 PM` on 143 of the 152 7-Year auctions since 2014 — the nine exceptions are all half-day sessions (six pre-Thanksgiving, two Christmas Eve, one unexplained 2016-02-26), and 2027-01-28 is an ordinary full Thursday, so the 1:00 p.m. ET close applies and the 11:30 a.m. close the treasury-7y-note-2026-11-25 ledger measured DOES NOT transfer here. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-21 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read its one prior proposal first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/treasury-7y-note-2027-01-28.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21.json, now shadowed and inert. The proposal's terms, size expectation and 1:00 p.m. close all survive re-derivation; its FOMC framing is the part this research tested. THIS IS THE LAST 7-YEAR ROW THE SCHEDULE PUBLISHES — the PDF's window terminates on 2027-02-04, so no successor is proposable from this primary and none is filed. FOMC POSITION: the 2027-01-26/27 meeting (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, re-fetched direct this session) puts this auction at D+1, the first coupon auction after the statement. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING — the straddle is a NULL on the auction and a REAL effect on the session, and those are different claims. Across the 16 7-Year auctions since 2014 that sold one session after a decision: bid-to-cover 2.487 vs 2.494 for the other 136 (Welch t = -0.21), and the residual against the inherited dealer model `7s10s = -1.894 + 0.090 x dealer%` is -0.260bp (t = -0.83) vs +0.031bp (Welch t = -0.88) — no extra concession on either channel. The cleanest control available: the 81 D+1 sessions with NO auction move 7s10s by -0.148bp (t = -0.89), statistically identical to the 16 D+1 auction days' -0.125bp, so the auction adds nothing to a day-after-FOMC session. WHAT IS REAL IS THE NOISE: session 7s10s standard deviation on D+1 is 1.493bp against 1.194bp on sessions more than three from a decision — a VARIANCE RATIO OF 1.56 — the |move| means are 1.072 vs 0.823bp (Welch t = 2.32), and the tail P(|d7s10s| >= 2bp) is 22.7% vs 11.8%. The same fitted ~-0.8bp effect therefore needs 28 auctions to detect on a D+1 session against 18 on an ordinary one. The practical output is that 2027-01-28 is the LEAST readable date in this tenor's calendar, and the reason is the denominator, not the crowd. THE JANUARY STRUCTURE IS THE NORM, NOT AN EVENT: 9 of the 13 January 7-Year auctions since 2014 sat within one session of an FOMC decision (6 exactly at D+1), because the January month-end coupon block and the January FOMC are both locked to the last week of the month. A MONTH-SPLIT TRAP WAS FOUND AND KILLED rather than reported as a finding: January D+1 residuals mean +0.571 (n=6) against non-January -0.759 (n=10, t = -2.14), but all 13 January auctions at any offset mean +0.030 (t = 0.09) and the non-January leg is carried by two members (2022-07-28 at -3.06, 2015-10-29 at -2.22) — one uncorrected cell of a post-hoc split. SIZE EXPECTATION $44B: 29 consecutive 7-Year auctions at that size, 2024-04-25 to 2026-08-27, the prior one $43B; the January-2027 cell is three months past the last row sb0590 publishes and is set at the 2026-11-04 refunding.
